summary: Round 5 delta is comment-only in production plus one test-fixture strengthening; I re-measured every number it asserts rather than accepting it. The unbounded series 29/46/80/148/284 at 1/2/4/8/16 prior terms is EXACT on this harness (measured in my own tree with crossFromCheckpoint forced to return false: total 29/46/80/148/284, gets 18/33/63/123/243, lists 3/4/6/10/18, stats 4/5/7/11/19, puts 4 throughout), and the bounded side is 17 at every term (gets 5, lists 3, stats 5, puts 4) -- so the row's 'become 17 and 17' and the three flat classes are all true. The rewritten ChainReplay note now attributes only the SHAPE to M4.6e's row, which that row does record verbatim ('per-failover cost is O(all commit-log entries ever written) ... M4.9's row now carries the measured table'), and attributes the numbers to this harness; the two-author ambiguity is gone. The two-burn fixture is correct: the walk goes 4 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1, terminates at epoch 1's checkpoint (sequence 41, one stat + one get through the LATEST pointer) and never reads epoch 1's forty deltas; 14 is exact (7 stats, 3 gets, 4 lists) and I derived it independently before running it. The strengthened isEqualTo(14L) kills the mutation it names: guarding the arithmetic-branch probe to fire only on the first step yields 52... 55 measured (expected 14, was 55) and disabling the crossing entirely yields 52 measured -- both figures the row publishes are exact. The offset assertion alone survives both mutants, which is why the count assertion is the load-bearing one. isLessThanOrEqualTo(15L) -> isEqualTo(14L) moves the threshold in the STRENGTHENING direction. Burning a second epoch changes nothing outside the test: the fixture owns its own MemoryBinStore, does not go through LocalSequencer.start or firstInheritableAncestor, and the full ./gradlew test is green in my tree, stable across three reruns. Request-rate lens: production behaviour is unchanged by this delta, so nothing new scales with records, shards, partitions or indices. One residual minor, non-blocking.

findings.title: The corrected bullet contradicts the bullet immediately above it, which still carries the retracted claim
findings.detail: The fix rewrote the SECOND bullet (lines 254-260) to say 'this and the burned-epoch count are the absolute numbers on the bounded path'. The FIRST bullet, four lines earlier and untouched, still says 'AN ABSOLUTE COUNT, not an equality between two measurements. Every other cost assertion HERE compares two runs'. 'Here' is this file, and this file now contains a second absolute cost assertion -- aRunOfBURNEDEpochsStillStopsAtTheCheckpointBehindThem's isEqualTo(14L), strengthened from an inequality in this same delta. So the two bullets state opposite things about the same file, and the one left standing is the one the fix was written to retract. Separately, the rewritten bullet says 'the TWO cost tests in the sibling suite compare two MEASUREMENTS'; LocalSequencerBoundedRecoveryTest has THREE cost tests, and the third (aPredecessorTOOSHORTToCheckpointStillStopsAtItsAncestorsCheckpoint) asserts isLessThanOrEqualTo(30L), an absolute bound rather than a comparison of two runs.
findings.recommendation: Record in the commit body rather than fix. This is the fifth instance of the milestone's own recurring shape (a correction leaving the corrected claim standing), and per review.md the next round's surface is the prose the fix just added. If it is fixed, the two bullets should be merged into one sentence, not qualified again.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer adding a third absolute count to this file reads the first bullet, believes absolute counts are unique here and relative comparisons are the house style, and either weakens the new assertion to a comparison of two runs -- which a recovery issuing six redundant requests satisfies, the exact hole the second bullet exists to close -- or deletes the second bullet as the contradictory one. Either way the comment that survives is the false one.
